A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCoTS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite relocated material and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCoTS planning and data-augmentation experiments, including OGBench results and controller, refinement and replanning analyses. Appendix D separately identifies externally sourced baseline scores.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds component ablations, sensitivity analyses, D4RL locomotion results and mobile robot navigation results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core stitching algorithm, objectives and refinement procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C adds limited task-specific adaptations: a learned reward predictor labels augmented dense-reward trajectories, and a pretrained beta-VAE encodes LiDAR occupancy images for navigation.

E1.justification: v3 retains the eight OGBench settings and adds Hopper and Walker2d medium/medium-replay datasets for dense-reward offline RL. It also evaluates noisy, partially observable LiDAR navigation in building and corridor environments, substantially extending task and input coverage.

E2.justification: Diffuser, previously discussed as prior work, becomes an evaluated comparator against Diffuser trained with SCoTS augmentation in Table 11. Comparator membership in the retained main experiments is unchanged; the navigation experiment reuses HIQL.

E3.justification: The original OGBench settings and Table 5 are unchanged. New protocols include component-removal controls and beta, segment-length and retrieval-count sweeps; D4RL normalized-return evaluation with horizon 32, segment length 4 and 2M samples; and navigation evaluation over 100 episodes using short-range collected trajectories and processed LiDAR observations.

E4.justification: v1 includes controller-horizon and replanning ablations, qualitative novelty comparisons and refinement Dynamic MSE analysis. v3 retains these and adds direct temporal-embedding ablation, downstream HD/HIQL refinement ablations, and quantitative sensitivity analyses for novelty weight, segment length and retrieved-candidate count (Tables 6–10).

E5.justification: Existing OGBench reporting remains five seeds, 50 episodes per task and standard deviations. The new D4RL results explicitly average over 50 planning seeds, adding a distinct seed-reporting protocol. Navigation results specify 100 episodes but do not clearly define their run count or reported uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their scores, while Tables 6–12 add substantial results. New comparisons include AntMaze-Giant-Stitch success of 7±2 without temporal embeddings versus 87±2 with them, D4RL average returns of 79.5 for Diffuser versus 87.2 with SCoTS, and building-navigation success of 27±7 for HIQL versus 53±4 with augmentation. These are newly reported comparisons, not revisions of earlier scores.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, temporal-distance formulation, expectile objective and stitching scores remain unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added; the new embedding discussion provides qualitative reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reward-free trajectory augmentation using temporal embeddings, exploratory stitching and diffusion refinement to improve diffusion planning and offline GCRL. The added experiments broaden supporting evidence without changing these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly argues that local retrieval does not require globally accurate temporal distances. Appendix C explains novelty-driven detours around embedding distortions, interprets parameter sensitivities, and clarifies that reward-free describes stitching rather than downstream reward use. The existing computational-cost and asymmetric-MDP limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New experiment details specify reward-model training on original offline data and navigation preprocessing from 512-ray LiDAR to 64×64 occupancy grids and eight-dimensional beta-VAE representations, with trajectories collected over 5m ranges. Existing architecture specifications, hyperparameter table, hardware, runtimes and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the new experiments and planning context, including beta-VAE, HRL navigation and Fast Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion. The central positioning against reward-guided augmentation and test-time trajectory composition is unchanged. Publication updates to existing references do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. v3 adds a methodological remark, notation clarification, Appendix C subsections, an impact statement and acknowledgements, alongside small language corrections and conference metadata. The code link moves to the abstract.

P2.justification: Appendix C gains a substantial suite of seven tables presenting component controls, parameter sweeps and additional benchmarks. Existing figures are retained; the novelty and long-horizon illustrations exchange order, Table 5 moves to a standalone page, and surrounding layouts reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the method's design and applicability. Tables 6–10 supply direct component and sensitivity tests where v1 relied partly on qualitative illustrations or indirect Dynamic MSE evidence. Dense-reward and LiDAR-navigation experiments test previously unexamined settings. These additions materially improve empirical support, although implementation and uncertainty reporting for the new navigation experiment remain limited.
